title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the end of a general section, before §50 'Exemple: le tour de Fermat', which studies a quotient of SL(2,Z)^ by [Π0,Π0]. The page continues a construction begun on the previous page.

Setup. 𝔊 is an abstract (discrete) group. Over a 'universal base' S0 (presumably Spec Z) there is a filtrant projective system of affine group schemes 𝔊_i, with affine transition maps. Its limit is a pro-affine group scheme LEnv(𝔊) over S0; the transcription's 'End'/'Ext' should most likely read 'Env', for enveloppe. By base change one gets a pro-S-group Env_S(𝔊) = (𝔊_{i,S})_i and its limit group scheme LEnv_S(𝔊) = LEnv(𝔊) ×_{S0} S.

On the previous page, (58) says: for G locally of finite presentation over S, homomorphisms of pro-objects Hom_{pro-S-gr}(Env_S(𝔊), G) := lim→_i Hom(𝔊_{i,S}, G) agree with homomorphisms from the limit scheme, Hom_{S-gr}(LEnv_S(𝔊), G). This is the usual EGA IV §8 limit argument. The canonical maps of constant group schemes 𝔊_{S0} → 𝔊_i give, by (59), a homomorphism 𝔊_S → LEnv_S(𝔊).

This page.
- (60): composing with (59) gives a map Hom_{S-gr}(LEnv_S(𝔊), G) → Hom_{S-gr}(𝔊_S, G). The target is ≅ Hom_gr(𝔊, Γ(G/S)) = Hom_gr(𝔊, G(S)), since 𝔊_S is the constant group scheme.
- (61): composing (58) and (60) gives a canonical map Hom_{pro-S-gr}(Env_S(𝔊), G) ≅ Hom_{S-gr}(LEnv_S(𝔊), G) → Hom_gr(𝔊, G(S)).

Theorem (being stated; the text runs onto the next sheet). Let 𝔊 be an arbitrary discrete group and G a group scheme locally of finite presentation over S. Then (61) is injective, and its image is a specified set of homomorphisms 𝔊 → G(S); the qualifying adjective is illegible. Grothendieck first wrote 'bijective' under extra hypotheses 'pour ne pas nous fatiguer', crossed it out, and replaced it with 'injective, and has as image …'. He then adds that, to simplify the existence part, he assumes S noetherian and G (probably) affine, or possibly finite, over S.

Interpretation. Env_S(𝔊) is a relative pro-algebraic envelope (hull, completion) of a discrete group over an arbitrary base, defined over Spec Z and base-changed. The theorem characterises which abstract homomorphisms 𝔊 → G(S) extend, necessarily uniquely, to the envelope. Over a field with all affine algebraic G, this is the Hochschild–Mostow pro-algebraic completion, where (61) is bijective. Over a general base it is plausibly an analogue for profinite or pro-finite-flat completions.

The purpose in the manuscript is presumably to give algebraic models over Z (or a cyclotomic base) of envelopes of discrete groups such as SL(2,Z) and its quotients (Fermat tower). These would serve Galois-Teichmüller-type questions in the Longue Marche continuation.
errors: The text is too fragmentary at the decisive point (the description of the image of (61)) to verify the theorem. As stated, injectivity requires that 𝔊_S → LEnv_S(𝔊) be schematically dominant in a suitable sense, i.e. that the envelope be generated by the image of 𝔊. This holds if the 𝔊_i are taken as closures or images of 𝔊, but cannot be checked from this page alone.

Grothendieck's own correction (bijective → injective with a described image) shows that bijectivity fails over a general base without restricting G or the homomorphisms. This is a self-corrected error, not a residual one.

ideas.what: Pro-affine group scheme envelope Env_S(𝔊) of a discrete group over an arbitrary base S, obtained by base change from a universal base S0, with a universal map from the constant group 𝔊_S
ideas.modern_name: Pro-algebraic (algebraic hull / Tannakian) completion of a discrete group, relative version over Z or a general base
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hochschild–Mostow (1957, over fields); later Deligne, Hain (relative completion); Tannakian versions over Dedekind rings (e.g. Wedhorn, Duong–Hai) much later
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; related to SGA 3 constant group schemes and Tannakian ideas (Saavedra's thesis under Grothendieck)

ideas.what: Identification of Hom from a pro-group to a group scheme locally of finite presentation with Hom from the projective limit scheme
ideas.modern_name: Limit argument for functors locally of finite presentation (EGA IV 8.14)

ideas.what: Theorem: the canonical map Hom_{pro-S-gr}(Env_S(𝔊), G) → Hom_gr(𝔊, G(S)) is injective with image a specified class of homomorphisms (S noetherian, G affine/finite for existence)
ideas.modern_name: Universal property / extension criterion for the relative pro-algebraic completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical over fields (Hochschild–Mostow); over general bases scattered later literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a pro-algebraic envelope of a discrete group over an arbitrary base S (defined over a universal base and base-changed). He states a characterisation of the abstract homomorphisms 𝔊 → G(S) extending to it, deliberately weakening 'bijective' to 'injective with image …'. This is followed immediately by an application to quotients of SL(2,Z) (Fermat tower), suggesting envelopes over Z or cyclotomic bases as tools for Galois actions on such groups.
missed.quote: l'application canonique (61) est injective, et a comme image ... homomorphismes de 𝔊 dans G(S) ... pour nous simplifier l'existence, que S est noeth. et G [affine] sur S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and relative pro-algebraic completions of discrete groups (e.g. of SL(2,Z) or modular groups over Z) are of current interest: motivic fundamental groups, integral Malcev completion, Tannakian groups over Dedekind rings. An early Grothendieck formulation over arbitrary bases, tied to the Fermat tower, would be a historical precedent. Its mathematical novelty is unclear given the illegible image description.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a natural, partly routine construction: a pro-algebraic envelope over a general base, plus a limit argument. The interesting part, the precise image of (61), is illegible. Envelopes of discrete groups are classical over fields, and relative or integral versions exist in later literature. It is mildly notable as evidence that Grothendieck was working with integral pro-algebraic completions in the Longue Marche continuation.
transcription_corrections: 'L Ext_S(𝔊)' and 'Ext_S(𝔊)' (and 'End' on the previous page) most likely read 'L Env_S(𝔊)' / 'Env_S(𝔊)' (enveloppe).
In (61) the left side reads 'Hom_{pro-S-gr}(Env_S(𝔊), G)'; the superscript after Hom is unclear. The final term is Hom_gr(𝔊, G(S)).
Theorem parenthesis: '(𝔊 groupe discret arbitraire, G schéma en groupes loc. de prés. finie sur schéma de base S)'.
Crossed-out text reads approximately: 'bijective dès qu'on suppose de plus, pour ne pas nous fatiguer, que'.
Last lines: '... — dès maintenant, pour nous simplifier l'existence, que S est noethérien et G affine (or: fini) sur S'.
First line: '𝔊_{S0} → 𝔊_i .' (end of the sentence from the previous page).
